docs.title: BillVault
docs.text: BillVault turns receipts and invoices into structured, reviewable data.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
• Takes documents in from an upload, a watched folder, a Dropbox or OneDrive account, or a scheduled poll, as PDF, image or XML (UBL / ZUGFeRD).
  • Extracts the fields with a fixed waterfall: invoice templates first, then an OCR service, then an AI service only when the earlier steps find nothing. Deterministic steps always run before any AI call.
  • Protects card data: card-number-shaped values in extracted text are detected, checked and redacted before anything is stored, and the receipt is flagged for review.
  • Keeps a person in charge: every extracted receipt goes to a review queue, with the reason it needs a look, and page operations (rotate, delete, reorder, split, merge) on the source documents.
  • Signs people in with Google, Microsoft, LinkedIn or GitHub.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• Architecture diagrams: how documents flow through the system and how sign-in works.
  • API reference: every endpoint and schema, generated from the running application.

docs.title: Architecture diagrams
docs.text:
These diagrams are generated by scripts/gen_diagrams.py. Three are written from the code and checked against it (docs/diagrams/src/); three are derived from the code itself so they cannot drift: the module map (Python imports), the database schema (SQLAlchemy metadata) and the tenant lifecycle (_ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS). Regenerate with uv run python scripts/gen_diagrams.py.

Every diagram is available as Mermaid (shown on its page, rendered natively by GitHub), SVG and Excalidraw. The interactive HTML version (pan, zoom, search, trace) opens correctly on the docs site; on GitHub a committed .html file would show its source, so link the docs-site page, not the file.

  • Module map: Which parts of app/ import which other parts, counted from the Python source (import statements, aggregated per component).
  • Ingestion pipeline: How a document gets from an upload, a directory, a scheduled poll or a cloud-storage account to a persisted Receipt.
  • Database schema: Every table and foreign key, read from the SQLAlchemy metadata in app/models.py (not typed by hand).
  • OAuth login and signup: The end-user sign-in flow for Google, Microsoft, LinkedIn (OIDC) and GitHub (OAuth2).
  • Tenant billing and provisioning (Phase 21): How a Stripe subscription event reaches the tenant registry, and where the Azure deployment stamp fits.
  • Tenant lifecycle: The states a tenant can be in and the moves the registry allows, read from _ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS in app/services/tenant_registry.py.

Waterfall order

  • XML first, then invoice2data templates, then the OCR gateway, then the AI gateway
  • Deterministic paths always win before any AI call

Failure handling

  • A transient gateway error retries the job after 30 s, up to 3 tries
  • In a directory batch one bad file is counted in receipts_failed and does not stop the others

Colour Meaning blue Route handler in app/api/auth_routes.py green Service function in app/services/oauth.py or a helper in auth_routes.py gray External identity provider orange Session state Node Detail GET /auth/login buttons for configured_providers() only GET /auth/{provider}/authorize 404 if unconfigured; redirect_uri pinned to oauth_redirect_base_url Provider consent Google, Microsoft, LinkedIn (OIDC discovery); GitHub (plain OAuth2) GET /auth/{provider}/callback authorize_access_token(): authorization code to tokens Profile GitHub: fetch_github_profile() with /user/emails fallback; others: userinfo then normalize_profile() _find_or_create_user() matched by email; 400 if the provider returns none _upsert_identity() OAuthIdentity(provider, provider_account_id) Session user_id and last_activity set; redirect to /me GET /me require_user: 401 without a valid session

One user, several providers

  • A user is matched by email, so signing in with a second provider using the same email lands on the same User
  • A provider that returns no email is rejected with 400

Configuration

  • Only providers with credentials in the environment appear on the login page
  • The callback URL is built from oauth_redirect_base_url, not from the request Host header
